root_cause_label: Agent deliberately omitted printing the 1000-variable solution vector and never saved it to a file, so the required output was never produced
one_sentence_failure_summary: After four scipy timeout failures, the agent pivoted to a one-step gradient descent but explicitly commented out the line that would have printed the solution vector, submitting only a cost reduction without ever outputting the 1,000 required variable values.
t_err_evidence: In step 10, the agent writes solve.py with the line `# print(f"Final x: {final_x}") # Don't print the full vector, it's too long` — deliberately suppressing the output of the solution and not adding any file-save mechanism, violating the task requirement to provide the 1,000 variable values.
t_commit_evidence: The script in step 10 has no mechanism to output or save the solution vector; once written and subsequently run in step 11, the outcome is locked in — the final answer will never contain the required variable values.
t_surface_evidence: Step 11 output shows only cost values ('Initial cost: 23183.6...', 'Final cost: 21571.9...') with no variable values printed, making the missing output observable.
trigger_explanation: The task explicitly requires the agent to provide the 1,000 variable values as output. The agent was aware of the existence of the solution vector (final_x) but chose to suppress its output with the comment 'Don't print the full vector, it's too long,' never saving it to a file either. This is a deliberate disregard of a core task requirement.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 3, 5, 7, and 9 all show empty terminal output (timeouts) from successive scipy optimization runs, signaling severe performance problems that forced the agent to pivot strategies.
